amendments.rule: The definite direct-object marker `אֵת` (H853) has no English realization of its own and is normally its own `unrepresented` unit; that is the ruling on the large majority of its occurrences. It takes English only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation itself and no other morpheme licenses that word. Three families qualify. An English verb may reach its object through a preposition — *hearken unto*, *spake unto*, *inquire of*, *fight against*, *send for* — where that preposition exists only to attach the object to the verb; it is the marker's rendering, not the object noun's, and the marker heads on it. An appositional or resumptive marker may be rendered *even* or *to wit*. **But only a marker standing on the very phrase that English word introduces.** Where the ASV writes an appositional *even* or *to wit* before a phrase no marker marks, no morpheme licenses it and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30, whatever markers stand elsewhere in the clause: `וְחַקּוֹתָ עָלֶיהָ עִיר אֵת־יְרוּשָׁלִָם` → *portray upon it a city,* ***even*** *Jerusalem* gives *even* to the marker, which stands on the appositive itself, while `נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֵת־שְׁנֵי עֲוֺנָם לְמִסְפַּר יָמִים שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵאוֹת וְתִשְׁעִים יוֹם` → *a number of days,* ***even*** *three hundred and ninety days* leaves the *even* `added`, because the clause's one marker stands on `שְׁנֵי עֲוֺנָם`, which the ASV renders bare. Do not reach across the clause for a marker to carry such a word, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*: the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. And a marker on an object the ASV fronts before its clause and resumes inside it with a pronoun may be rendered *as for*: `וְאֶת־הַיְבוּסִי יוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם לֹא־יָכְלוּ בְנֵי־יְהוּדָה לְהוֹרִישָׁם` → *And* ***as for*** *the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out* gives *as for* to the marker, headed on *as* by rule 24, since the resuming *them* is the suffix's under rule 18 and nothing else answers to the two words. Test by subtraction: drop the English word and ask which morpheme has lost its rendering. If nothing but the object relation is diminished, the marker takes the word; if the ASV writes the object bare — *he built the house* — the marker is `unrepresented`. Do not confuse H853 with its homograph the preposition `אֵת` *with* (H854), which is an ordinary preposition aligning by rule 11.
amendments.why: Rule 16 licenses an *even* for an appositional marker but never says what becomes of an appositional *even* that no marker stands on, and it offers only `unrepresented` as the marker's other outcome. EZK.4 held all three cases at once — one marker on its own appositive (4.1) and two clauses whose markers stand on earlier bare-rendered objects while the ASV writes *even* before a numeral apposition (4.5, 4.9) — and both `added` units had to reason the disposition out at length because the contract did not carry it. The amendment adds only that qualification and its `added` disposition, in the same shape rules 42, 51 and 55 already use for a surplus *and*, *also* and *if*; it narrows nothing the corpus has aligned, since the corpus's 23 `אֵת` → *even* units are markers on their own appositives and the default remains the 4039 `unrepresented` ones. The rest of the rule is returned verbatim, including the three families, the *as for* precedent and its head, the subtraction test and the H854 warning.

conventions: An English *even* is aligned to an `אֵת` only where that marker stands on the phrase the word introduces. EZK.4.1's `אֵת־יְרוּשָׁלִָם` → *portray upon it a city, even Jerusalem* takes it under rule 16; the appositional *even* before *three hundred and ninety days* in EZK.4.5 and EZK.4.9 is `added` under rule 30, because each clause's only markers stand on earlier objects the ASV renders bare, and neither is reached across the clause to avoid the `added`. EZK.4.13's *Even thus* is not this construction: *thus* alone is the whole of `כָּכָה`'s rendering and *Even* completes the ASV's emphatic expression rather than introducing an apposition, so it joins that morpheme's unit under rule 31; that verse's note names the competing `added` reading.

`מִסְפַּר הַיָּמִים` → *according to the number of the days* (EZK.4.4, EZK.4.9) is read as one compound judgment in both verses. The italicized *according to* goes to the construct `מִסְפָּר` as the function words its adverbial accusative licenses under rule 33, and is not `added`; the ASV's two *the*s are then distributed by rule 29's arthrous-rectum clause, the present article on `הַיָּמִים` taking the one standing before *days* and the construct taking a supplied one. Nothing is fronted here, unlike EZK.4.11's `שִׁשִּׁית הַהִין` → *the sixth part of a hin*, where the ASV writes a single *the* and the present article takes it.

report: Checked all 37 candidate lemma groups, plus the dump read end to end for `added`-versus-folded asymmetries the lemma table is blind to. No split found; patches is empty.

`קַח־לְךָ` (EZK.4.1, 4.3, 4.9) is the sharpest-looking candidate and is not a split: the ASV writes *unto thee* in 4.3 and 4.9 and bare *take thee* in 4.1, so rule 40's condition — whether an English word is spent on what the preposition contributes — settles each independently. The datives of 4.9 (*make thee*) and 4.15 (*given thee*) go the same way.

The four English *even*s are the one place a later reader will stop. Three are appositional and divide on whether a marker stands on the appositive: EZK.4.1's `אֵת־יְרוּשָׁלִָם` does, so the marker takes the word under rule 16; in EZK.4.5 and EZK.4.9 each clause's only markers stand on earlier objects the ASV renders bare, so the word is `added` under rule 30. EZK.4.13's *Even thus* is a different construction — an intensifier beside the single word rendering `כָּכָה`, taken into that morpheme's unit under rule 31 — and its note names the competing `added` reading. Recorded as a convention, and rule 16 is amended so the disposition is not rediscovered.

Articles are uniform: a present morpheme takes a written *the* (4.3, 4.4, 4.9, 4.11, 4.13), goes `unrepresented` where the ASV writes none (4.3, 4.6, 4.10, 4.12, 4.15), and yields to a suffix that takes the phrase's single determiner (4.4, 4.6, rule 41). `מִסְפַּר הַיָּמִים` is read identically in 4.4 and 4.9; `לְמִסְפַּר יָמִים` in 4.5 differs only because no article morpheme is present there.

Waw renderings — *also*, *And*, *Moreover*, *For*, *so*, *Then*, *with*, *for*, *or*, *even*, and the `unrepresented` apodosis waw of 4.6 — are each read off the ASV under rule 14, and both numeral waws (4.5, 4.9) take the *and* standing between *hundred* and *ninety*. Verbs, suffixes, supplied copulas and supplied *the*/*of*/*a* are uniform throughout.

BSB 93.1%: no genuine error. The counted classes are documented convention differences — object markers (rule 16), prepositions the ASV's recasting silences (rule 40), the repeated `בֵּין` (rule 26), articles (rules 29/41) — and the 4.3 `בַ` is the `הָיָה בְ` recasting the contract itself names as the prophets' usual source of this disagreement (rule 21). The four content disagreements (4.6's unrendered second `יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה`, 4.8's two `צַד` suffixes, 4.10's gapped resumptive suffix, 4.12's fronted `הִיא`) are places where the ASV writes one English word for two Hebrew morphemes; each carries a note. Nothing changed to improve the rate.

Two judgments left standing that a later reader should know are deliberate, both noted in their verses: EZK.4.6 marks the supplied *when* `added` on rule 55's contiguity test, because `שֵׁנִית`'s fronted *again* stands between it and the waw's *And*; and EZK.4.6 renders the doubled distributive `יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה יוֹם לַשָּׁנָה` on its first occurrence, leaving the whole second phrase `unrepresented` under rule 22. Rule 22 does not say which occurrence a repeated non-numeral phrase renders, but one verse is too thin to promote a rule from, so I left the contract alone.
